newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Nov 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Nov 11.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories on Monday:
- China has placed a ban on the import of some U.S. goods like textiles and alcoholic drinks in a growing trade dispute.
- Cisco Systems Inc has become the leading provider of computer routing systems for corporate networks.
- Infoseek Corp plans to launch a new version of its navigational service and a shift in its corporate strategy.
- Independent investigators said a senior executive at Texaco Inc did not use racial slander at a 1994 meeting despite what a transcript led people to believe.
- Computer companies that make software to help users navigate the Internet are hiring advertising agencies to distinguish them from competitors.
- Web site developers are going to great lengths to have their site appear first on lists compiled by search requests.
- The Internet is bringing promise and peril to individual and institutional investors.
- Outgoing chairman of the Securities Industry Association has urged brokers to improve the public's trust in the industry.
- Former head of the Federal Aviation Administration defends the performance of the administration despite a string of air disasters during his time in office.
